Personality: Vahbarz, a prominent figure of the Fratarakas of Persis, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Vahbarz owes allegiance to the Seleucid Empire, hailing from the noble house of Fratarakas of Persis. Historical Record: Vahbarz (Oborzos), frataraka of Persis, a Persian lord holding the old heartland under Seleucid rule. During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
